Suzuki coupling for preparation of allenes-ligand effect and 
chirality transfer 
Hongwen Luoa, Yihua Yub and Shengming Mac,d 
A general and efficient palladium-catalyzed coupling of propargylic carbonates with organoboronic acids has been 
developed by identifying a commercially available semi-labile bidentated o-(diphenylphosphino)benzaldehyde as the 
effective ligand affording allenes under a set of very mild reaction conditions. Many functional groups are tolerated in this 
reaction, and high chirality transfer has also been realized in the presence of water leading to a very rapid reaction for the 
synthesis of easily recemized 1,3-diarylallenes. A rationale has been proposed for the role of the ligand.
Introduction 
Allenes are present in many natural products and have been 
recognized as very useful building blocks in organic synthesis 
nowadays.1,2 Consequently, extensive studies have been focused on 
efficient methods for the synthesis of different types of allenes. 2j,3 
Palladium-catalyzed coupling of propargylic compounds with 
organometallic reagents, 4 such as Grignard reagents, 5 
organoaluminum reagents, 6 organoindium reagents, 7 organozinc 
reagents,5b,6a,8 organocopper reagents,5b organosilver reagents, 5b 
organotin reagents, 6a,9 and organosilicone reagents,10 is one of the 
most useful and efficient methodology to synthesize allenes.  
However, some organometallic reagents are unstable, expensive, 
and toxic. Although related reports on utilizing these easily available 
mild organoboronic compounds have been reported, a temperature 
above 60 oC is  required in most of those studies, which may be 
troublesome for the easy racemizing  nature of allenes  (Scheme 1, 
a):11,12 Thus, rep ort on the  efficient chirality transfer using 
optically active propargylic derivatives for such allene syntheses are 
very limited. Molander and Yoshida independently  reported that a 
decent level of chirality transfer in the coupling reaction of 
propargylic phosphates with potassium trifluoroborates 12a or 
terminal propargylic carbonates with aryl boronic acids ,11f however, 
in majority cases, serious racemization or lower efficiency of 
chirality transfer was observed . The challenges are the ready 
racemization of propargylic/allenylic palladium intermediates  
through the  σ-π-σ isomerization process 13 and the sensitivity of 
allenes (see also Scheme 4).  With our goal of developing 
asymmetric synthesis of allenes, we wish to develop such a coupling 
reaction using commercially available boronic acids under ambient 
conditions (Scheme 1, b).  
 
 
Scheme 1  Pd-catalyzed coupling protocols of propargylic 
derivatives with organoboronic compounds. 
 
As we know, the formyl group (CH=O) has been explored for 
its coordinatio n ability with transition metals, such as  Ru, Rh, 
Re, Cu, and Pd .14 However, to the best of our  knowledge, only 
very few studies employed those complexes as catalysts have 
been reported, 15 probably due to the high reactivity or 
sensitivity of aldehyde func tionality under different reaction 
conditions. In this report, we wish to disclose that the 
commercially available o-(diphenylphosphino)benzaldehyde 
has been identified as the effective ligand for the allene 
synthesis under very mild reaction conditions wi th a very wide 
scope both for arylboronic acids and propargylic carbonates . In

Results and Discussion 
In our initial studies, 7 -chloro-1-phenylhepta-2-yn-1-yl methyl 
carbonate 1a and phenylboronic acid 2a were used as the 
prototypical substrates for optimization of reaction conditions . 
When a mixture of 1a and 2a was treated with Pd2(dba)3·CHCl3 
(2 mol%) and PPh 3 (8 mol%) in dioxane at 30 oC for 12 h, only 
6% yield of the corresponding allene product 3aa was obtained 
(Scheme 2). Although electron -rich ligand L1 gave 64% yield of 
product 3aa, other monodentate ligands, such as TFP  and 
P(p-Tol)3 failed to promote the reaction smoothly. Then, we 
studied the effect of bidentate liga nds. SPhos with OMe as the 
flexible coordination site provided an acceptable yield of 
product 3aa with 18% of recovery, however, ligand L2 and 
Zheda-Phos failed in the reaction. To our surprise, the 
commercially available bidentate monophosphine , 
o-(diphenylphosphino)benzaldehyde ( L3),16 which has an 
interesting highly reactive formyl unit in the frame work, 
performed efficiently offering the highest yield of 90%. Control 
experiments showed that commonly available  bisphosphine 
ligand, such as Ph 2P(CH2)nPPh2 (n = 1 -4), dppf, rac-BINAP, 
Xantphos, and DPEPhos, afford a result of less than 11% yield, 
indicating the unique role of the formyl group. 
   After identifying L3 as the efficient ligand, other 
parameters were then investigated  (Table 1) . Although 
Pd(OAc)2 afforded 3aa with 77% yield, PdCl 2 and [Pd(allyl)Cl] 2 
were both ineffective for the  present transformation, yielding 
only trace quantity of the  targeted product (Table 1, entries 
1-3). No better results were obtained in toluene, DCE, or THF 
(Table 1, entries 5-7). We also studied the reactivity of other

Based on these data , we believe that the overall catalytic 
cycle requires the help of the rather  flexible coordination 
ability of the formyl group (Scheme  7):25 with the hemilabile 
nature of this ligand, the coordination -unsaturated Pd(0)-L3 
complex I would undergo SN2'-type oxidative addition with 
propargylic carbonates in an anti-stereospecific manner to 
give the tetra -coordinated stereodefined allenylic palladium 
intermediate II. The bidentate lig and helps to keep this 
palladium intermediate II coordination-saturated, which 
avoids any possible racemization through the  
isomerization process  while still keeping the reactivity for the 
transmetalation. Subsequently, intermediate II underwent 
transmetalationwith arylboronic acids through the four -center 
transition states III  by releasing the flexible coordination of 
the C=O unit. Water is facilating this step. Upon elimination of 
B(OH)2OMe, the C=O bites back to form intermediate IV. 
Subsequent reductive elimination afforded the coupling 
product 3 and regenerates the catalytically active palladium(0) 
complex I. 
Conclusions 
In summary, we have developed a general and efficient 
catalyst system consisting of a hemilabile formyl -containing 
P,O-ligand, i.e., o-(diphenylphosphino)benzaldehyde, for the 
coupling reaction of propargylic carbonates with stable and  
commercially av ailable arylboronic acids. The catalyst system 
functions under very mild conditions in absence of any base. A 
variety of useful functional groups are compatible with these 
reaction conditions  to afford  trisubstituted allenes, even 
tetrasubstituted allenes facilely. In addition, high ly efficient 
central-to-axial chirality transfer is also realized with the help 
of water. Further studies on the details of the reaction 
mechanism as well as the asymmetric protocol are in progress 
in our laboratory.
